description: Fetch property claims for a Wikidata entity with qualifier and reference detail. Item QIDs and quantity units — in values, qualifiers, and references — are resolved to human-readable labels by default. Use the properties parameter to fetch only specific P-IDs — omitting it returns every statement, and a well-connected item (a country, a major city) carries hundreds of properties: more than fits inline. A set over 24,000 bytes before labels comes back as kind: "outline" — every available P-ID with its byte size, largest first — instead of the statements; re-call with the same id plus properties:[...] naming P-IDs whose sizes sum to 24,000 or less (the retrieval_notice names one such set). Labels are added after that check, so a returned set can run past 24,000 bytes by their size, and a property requested alone is always returned whole — on a major item one property can run to hundreds of kilobytes. Designed for fact verification: "what does Wikidata say about this entity's {property}?". Preferred rank marks the favored statements for a property; check qualifiers and references for temporal scope and evidence.

id.description: Q-ID (e.g., "Q76") or P-ID of the entity to fetch statements for.

language.description: Wikidata language code for label resolution of QID values (e.g., "en", "de"). Case-insensitive; "_" is read as "-"; blank means "en".

properties.description: P-IDs to fetch (e.g., ["P31", "P569", "P27"]). Omit to return all properties (may be large for major items).

resolve_labels.description: Resolve item QIDs (label) and quantity unit QIDs (unitLabel) to human-readable labels via one batched label call, covering main values, qualifiers, and reference parts. Set to false to skip label resolution and return raw QIDs only (faster, smaller payload).

name: wikidata_get_statements

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `entity_not_found`: No entity exists at this ID — either unassigned or out of range. `invalid_id`: ID is not a valid Q-ID or P-ID format. `invalid_property`: A properties entry is not a valid P-ID format. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

id.description: The entity ID whose statements were fetched.

kind.description: full — statements carries the claims. outline — the statement set overflowed the inline byte budget, so sections lists the P-IDs available instead; re-call with properties:[...] to retrieve specific ones. The counts below are reported either way.

labelsResolved.description: True when the returned statements had labels resolved: resolve_labels was true and kind is full, so every item QID and quantity unit that resolved carries its label. False when resolve_labels was false, and on an outline, which carries no statements and makes no label lookup.

propertyCount.description: Number of distinct properties — those returned in full mode, those offered as sections in outline mode.

retrieval_notice.description: Present when kind = outline: how to re-call for specific properties.

sections.description: Present when kind = outline: the P-IDs this entity carries statements for, largest first, each sized as the UTF-8 bytes it adds to a response before labels. Sizes add up: copy names whose sizes sum to 24,000 or less into the properties input to retrieve them.

items.description: An available property — its P-ID and the serialized byte size of its statements.

bytes.description: Serialized byte size of the section

name.description: Section identifier — pass in `sections` to retrieve it

statementCount.description: Total number of statement objects across all properties. Counted before any overflow, so it reports the entity's full statement volume in both modes.

statements.description: Map of property ID to array of normalized statements. Each statement has id, rank, property, value (with type-specific fields), optional qualifiers ([{ property, value }]), and optional references — one entry per source in upstream order, each { parts: [{ property, value }] }. Present in full mode; omitted in outline mode.

title: Get Wikidata Statements
